admission.justification: The PATH node and the Eve Node were both weighed and rejected with reasons, and every future platform or Node bump has to change the contract and its archive entries.

alternatives.option: The contract names one exact Node release and, per supported platform, the official archive URL and SHA-256; the product fetches into its cache, verifies the digest, unpacks beside the target and moves it into place.
alternatives.reason: A release-owned, digest-checked Node is reproducible independently of what a user's shell file puts on PATH, and the same Node is provably the one the supervisor and worker run on (/proc/<pid>/exe).

alternatives.option: Use the node the user's shell puts on PATH, checking only its major version.
alternatives.reason: The PATH depends on the process that runs a command, the node is updated outside any product release, and the failure it produced named the wrong thing.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host ships its own Node or the supported platform gains a guaranteed system Node the build can verify.

alternatives.option: Reuse the Eve application's Node line (24 or newer).
alternatives.reason: The host was shown on 22.23.2 and on no other; the two applications were not examined for one shared Node, and the host is explicitly not required to share the Eve Node.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host declares support for the Eve line and one installed Node can serve both applications.

consequences: Supported platforms are Linux x86_64 with /proc; other platforms return a named unsupported result and install nothing.
The product writes under its data folder, its cache folder and two temporary paths; it changes no PATH, no shell file, no bin link and no npm configuration.
context: The host command line starts with `#!/usr/bin/env -S node ...`, the provision started npm by name and the bridge took shutil.which('node'); a machine without a PATH node reported the failure as 'the Paseo CLI is not installed'. This machine has two user-installed Node trees and /usr/bin holds none.
decider: architect's direction under D75, frozen in MIK-R96@v1 rule 3
